messages:
Alex F (infra): Quick heads-up — our EDP billing for March/Apr shows ~15% fewer reserved GPU hours being attributed to our account vs infra telemetry. That’s ~120k variance. Can someone from the vendor side confirm metering boundaries?
Maria G (finance): Oof. Can you paste the invoice lines and the meter SKUs? I want to see whether it’s a SKU mapping issue or actual metering.
Alex F (infra): Pasting simplified snippet (sanitized):
```
Invoice: INV-2027-03-1123
SKU: GPU_T4_RESERVED - billed_hours: 12,800
SKU: GPU_T4_ONDEMAND - billed_hours: 1,950
SKU: GPU_V100_PREEMPT - billed_hours: 420
Total billed GPU hours: 15,170
Internal telemetry (cluster-sum): 17,900 reserved-equivalent hours
Variance: 2,730 hours (~15%)
```
Jordan L (eng-ops): Looks like during two 3hr incidents (2027-03-09, 2027-04-06) scheduler fell back to on-demand/alternate SKU, but our autoscaler should have used reserved capacity first. Might be SKU substitution for availability reasons.
Sam P (sales): @AWS Rep can you confirm if reserved pool metering is strictly per-SKU? We need to know if fallbacks to a compatible but different SKU break EDP attribution.
AWS Rep (aws-sales): Thanks — we see the ticket. Quick Q: which account/linked-billing ID and the exact invoice number? Also, do you have the resource IDs or tags? We can check the internal usage mapping. :eyes:
Maria G (finance): Account: rw-inference-prod-03, BillingAccount: 987654321, Invoice INV-2027-03-1123 and INV-2027-04-1109. Resource tags included: redwood:cluster, rw:env=prod.
AWS Rep (aws-sales): Got it. Initial look shows some usage mapped to on-demand pool because instances launched under a different placement group (fallback due to AZ constrained) — those don't auto-attach to the reserved SKU. We can file a metering true-up for hours where capacity was available but inventory routing caused on-demand provisioning. Need a list of timestamps and instance IDs to speed it.
Alex F (infra): Will export instance events — but note: we deliberately have fallback policy to avoid request failures; we expect those fallback hours to be counted against our commitment as per EDP language. The current EDP we signed says "compatible substitutions allowed" but meter mapping unclear.
Jordan L (eng-ops): Proposed ask to vendor: (1) one-time credit for the 2,730 hours that were effectively our reserved usage, (2) clarification + amendment to EDP metering to include cross-SKU compatibility mapping, (3) a change in invoice breakdown with machine-readable usage API so we can reconcile automatically.
Sam P (sales): Also push for a temporary SKU holdback waiver for March-April so we don't get dinged for early termination/overage churn while they investigate. That’s a low-effort ask they sometimes grant.
AWS Rep (aws-sales): I can escalate to metering team. Action items from our side: open a support case referencing this thread, attach instance IDs and the two invoice PDFs. We can request a retroactive adjustment and a billing credit review. We’ll also ask product to confirm how compatible SKU substitution is treated in committed metering.
Maria G (finance): I'll send PDFs + CSV of instance IDs within 30m. Also pushing internal ask: don't pay disputed lines until resolved.
Alex F (infra): Also want to lock in an SLA amendment: if provider routes us off-reserved due to AZ capacity, we want (a) automatic metering under commitment or (b) a documented burst pool that won’t break commitment attribution.
AWS Rep (aws-sales): Noted. I'll include that in the escalation. Expect an initial update in 48-72h. If we can reproduce mapping mismatch, metering team often grants a one-off adjustment and then proposes the wording change for the EDP.
Jordan L (eng-ops): For our reconciliation, I'll dump a 7-day sample of instance lifecycle logs (start/stop/placement decisions) to the share and tag @AWS Rep there.
Sam P (sales): I'll coordinate the commercial ask: retro credit + EDP amendment + temporary holdback waiver. Also suggest asking for a 6mo grace window for any similar mapping issues while new metering rules are in place.
AWS Rep (aws-sales): Sounds good. Please create a support case and post the case ID here when done. I'll flag it as high priority and loop metering & account teams. :+1:
Alex F (infra): Thanks all — Maria/Jordan will post artifacts, Sam will lead the negotiation ask, and I’ll monitor infra diffs. Leaving here for the thread; ping if vendor responds. :raised_hands:
